name: John Steinbeck
hook: California's Nobel laureate: Dust Bowl migrants, Monterey canneries, and a poodle named Charley.

facts.label: John Steinbeck
facts.statement: John Steinbeck (1902–1968), a Californian who won the 1962 Nobel Prize in Literature, set much of his fiction in the Salinas Valley.

facts.label: The Grapes of Wrath
facts.statement: The Grapes of Wrath (1939) follows the Joad family from the Dust Bowl to California; its title comes from "The Battle Hymn of the Republic".

facts.label: Of Mice and Men
facts.statement: Of Mice and Men (1937), first called "Something That Happened", follows George and Lennie, who dream of rabbits on their own farm.

facts.label: East of Eden
facts.statement: East of Eden (1952) retells Cain and Abel through the Trask family, with Cathy Ames abandoning her sons Cal and Aron.

facts.label: Cannery Row
facts.statement: Cannery Row (1945) is set in Monterey, and Steinbeck wrote the sequel Sweet Thursday.

facts.label: The Pearl
facts.statement: The Pearl (1947) is about Kino, a diver who finds a great pearl and learns to be careful what he wishes for.

facts.label: Travels with Charley
facts.statement: Travels with Charley (1962) recounts his road trip across America with his poodle, Charley.
